Done — all three tracked files are back to their committed state (`git status` now shows no modifications).

What I did and why:

- **The "whole tree" refactor touched only 3 files**: `README.md`, `java-gson/.git-blame-ignore-revs`, and `java-gson/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md`. Each had the same junk appended — a blank line plus `// experiment: <its own path>`. Nothing else was modified, and nothing was staged.
- **Restored those 3 files** with `git restore`, which matches your ask exactly.
- **Left `ClaudeFlash/` alone.** It's untracked (`ClaudeFlash/sessions/75235181-...`) and is this session's own scratch data, not refactor output. `git clean` would have deleted it, so I scoped the restore to the tracked files instead. Remove it yourself if you want it gone.

One note worth flagging: there were no stashes and the changes were uncommitted, so discarding them was irreversible. I saved the diff to `discarded-refactor.patch` in the session scratchpad first in case you want to inspect what the tool did — `git apply` it to bring the junk back.
